stem: What are the 4Ps of the marketing mix?

options.content: Product, price, place and promotion
People, profit, planning and payment
Program, password, printer and power
Plan, produce, protect and pay

explanation: The 4Ps are product, price, place and promotion.

stem: A software firm offers a free one-month trial to schools and advertises at a head teachers' meeting. Which P do these actions mainly belong to?

options.content: Promotion
options.rationale: Correct: they make customers aware of the product.

options.content: Product design
Price
options.rationale: A trial does not change the price list.

options.content: Place
options.rationale: Place is about where and how customers obtain the product.

stem: What is market research?

options.content: Selling products at a market stall
Collecting and analysing information about customers, competitors and the market
Printing posters for a product
Copying a competitor's product and its price exactly in order to sell more to the same customers

stem: A shop adds a mark-up of 20% to the cost of an item. Which pricing method is this?

options.content: Copying the competitor's price
options.rationale: The method here depends on the shop's own cost.

options.content: Pricing by customer demand only
options.rationale: The method here depends on cost.

options.content: Free pricing
options.rationale: A mark-up is added, so the price is not free.

options.content: Cost-plus pricing

stem: A questionnaire is given only to learners at one small school. Why might the results mislead a business that plans to sell nationally?

options.content: Questionnaires cannot be used for research
Questionnaires always give the same answers
A questionnaire must be answered by a single person
The sample may not represent all the customers

explanation: A sample should represent the market.
hints: Who is missing from the sample?

stem: What does the conversion rate of an online advert measure?

options.content: How many times the advert was shown to the people online
options.rationale: That is the number of views.

options.content: The cost of each click
The share of the people who clicked that went on to buy
The size of the advert's picture
options.rationale: Picture size is not a conversion measure.

hints: Which two numbers does it compare?

stem: An innovator in Harare has invented a new device and wants to share the design with a possible partner. Which step best safeguards the idea?

options.content: Publish the full design on a public web site first so that people can see it
Sign a confidentiality agreement with the partner before sharing details
Tell everyone the idea at a public meeting
Wait to see if a competitor builds it

explanation: Confidentiality agreements protect ideas that are shared.
hints: How can the partner be bound to keep it secret?

stem: A small firm spends all its marketing money on social media posts but its product is hard to find and costs more than similar products. Which comment is the best evaluation?

options.content: Promotion alone decides success, so the product, price and place do not matter at all
Social media cannot be used for marketing
options.rationale: Social media is a valid channel.

options.content: The mix is unbalanced: promotion cannot make up for poor place and price, so all four Ps need attention
Because the product is new, it needs no price
options.rationale: A price is part of the mix.

hints: Which of the Ps are weak?

stem: A survey in which many people say they would buy a product guarantees that they will buy it.
explanation: False. Stated intentions are a guide, but people may not buy when the time comes.

stem: Match each P to an example for a school software supplier.

right.content: Direct sales by visiting schools and payment by mobile money
A demonstration at the district meeting and a free trial
Software that records attendance and works on one computer
A yearly licence fee per school

explanation: Each P answers a different question.

stem: Complete the sentences.

payload.template: The name, logo and reputation that make a product recognisable is its {{blank:a}}. A price found by adding a percentage to the cost is {{blank:b}} pricing. Sales divided by clicks, as a percentage, is the {{blank:c}} rate.

stem: Name the research method in which many people answer the same set of written questions.
200 learners were asked whether they would buy a revision app. 90 said yes, 70 said maybe and 40 said no. Calculate the percentage who said yes.
An item costs US\$7.50 to make. The owner adds a mark-up of 30%. Calculate the selling price, in US dollars.
hints: Mark-up = cost × percentage; price = cost + mark-up.

stem: An online advert is shown 8000 times and receives 240 clicks. Calculate the click-through rate.
Explain the 4Ps of the marketing mix for a business that sells a mobile app. [4]

points.description: Product: the features of the app that meet the needs of customers
Price: how much customers pay, for example a one-off fee
Place: where and how customers get the app, such as an app store or mobile money payment
Promotion: how customers are told about the app, such as social media, demonstrations or word of mouth

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Product: the features of the app that meet customers' needs. Price: the fee customers pay, for example a one-off fee. Place: where customers get the app, such as an app store or by mobile money. Promotion: how they are told about it, such as social media, demonstrations or word of mouth.

explanation: One mark for each P applied.
hints: Name each P and say what it means for the product.

stem: Describe two methods of market research that a new internet cafe could use. [4]

points.description: Questionnaire: ask many people what services they would use and what they would pay
It gives numbers that can be counted and compared
Observation or interviews: watch how people use other cafes, or ask a few people for detailed views
It shows what customers do or think in more detail

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A questionnaire asks many people what services they would use and what they would pay, giving numbers that can be counted. Interviews or observation show in more detail how people use other cafes or what they think.

hints: Two methods with a strength or use for each.

stem: A learner plans a small business that repairs phones and tablets for learners at a school in Mutare. Outline a simple marketing plan for it. [6]

points.description: An objective, for example to repair 40 devices in the first term
The target market: learners and teachers at the school
Product: the repair service and a guarantee
Price: a fair price for each repair, perhaps with a discount for groups
Place and promotion: a repair desk at school, mobile money payment, posters and word of mouth
How success will be measured, for example the number of repairs, customer feedback and profit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Objective: repair 40 devices in the first term. Target market: learners and teachers at the school. Product: phone and tablet repairs with a guarantee. Price: a fair price per repair with a group discount. Place and promotion: a repair desk at school with mobile money payment, posters and word of mouth. Success is measured by the number of repairs, customer feedback and profit.

explanation: The parts of a simple plan.
hints: Objective, target market, the four Ps, budget and how success is measured.

stem: Evaluate the use of social media advertising by a small business in Zimbabwe. [4]

points.description: Advantage: low cost to start and can reach many people
Advantage: results can be measured, for example clicks and sales
Disadvantage: customers need data and a smartphone, so some are not reached
Disadvantage: fake accounts, scams or bad comments can harm the brand; conclusion that it is useful alongside other methods

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Social media advertising costs little to start, reaches many people and can be measured by clicks and sales. However, customers need data and smartphones, so some are not reached, and scams or bad comments can harm the brand. It is useful alongside other methods such as posters and word of mouth.

hints: Compare advantages and disadvantages of digital marketing for a small business.

stem: A shop in Gweru sells an item for US\$9.75 that costs it US\$7.50. It pays US\$30 for an online advert that is shown 5000 times. The advert receives 150 clicks and leads to 12 sales.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the conversion rate of the advert.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the cost per sale of the advert, in US dollars.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the profit or loss of the campaign, in US dollars. Give a loss as a negative number.
parts.workedSolution:
1. Revenue = 12 × 9.75 = US\$117.
2. Cost of goods = 12 × 7.5 = US\$90.
3. Profit = 117 − 90 − 30 = US\$-3, a loss.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Suggest two ways in which the shop could make the next campaign profitable.

points.description: Improve the advert or target it better so that more of the clicks become sales
Lower the advert cost, or raise the price, or lower the cost of the item

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Target the advert better so that more clicks become sales, and lower the advert cost or raise the price or lower the cost of the item.

parts.explanation: Raise sales per advert or lower costs.

explanation: The campaign makes a loss of US\$3 because the revenue is US\$117, the goods cost US\$90 and the advert US\$30.
hints: Revenue = sales × price; cost of goods = sales × cost.
Profit = revenue − cost of goods − advert cost.

stem: Tatenda opens a shop in Bulawayo that sells and repairs second-hand laptops for students.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Describe two market research methods Tatenda could use before opening.

points.description: A questionnaire to students about what they would buy and what they can pay
Visiting competing shops to compare prices and services (observation)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A questionnaire to students about what they would buy and what they can pay, and visiting competing shops to compare prices and services.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Explain how he could choose a selling price for a laptop that cost him US\$150.

points.description: Add a mark-up to the cost, for example 30%, so that all costs are covered and a profit is made
Compare with competitors' prices and what students can afford, and adjust

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Add a mark-up to the cost, for example 30%, to cover costs and make a profit, and compare with competitors' prices and what students can afford.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Suggest two promotion methods for the shop.

points.description: Posters and demonstrations at colleges and schools
A social media page or messaging group with photographs and prices

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Posters and demonstrations at colleges and schools, and a social media page or messaging group with photographs and prices.

explanation: Each P is applied to a laptop repair and sales shop.
hints: Relate each P to the product.

stem:
A questionnaire about a new learning app was answered by 250 learners.

| Answer | Number of people |
|:-:|:-:|
| Yes | 100 |
| Maybe | 95 |
| No | 55 |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage who answered maybe.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage who answered no.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: The developer says: "40% will buy, so I should expect to sell to 40% of all learners." Explain two weaknesses in this conclusion.

points.description: Saying yes in a survey does not mean that people will actually buy
The learners asked may not be a representative sample of all learners
